title: Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship
program_type: University-administered, industry-sponsored stipend scholarship awarded on a separate application submitted at admission
implementing_agency: RMIT University Sponsorship Development Team, with Medibank as the industry sponsor
programme_action: RMIT scholarship for commencing international students - Medibank-sponsored tier
description: The Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship is an RMIT University scholarship sponsored by Medibank, available to international students studying Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia. The scholarship has a total value of AU$20,000, paid to the recipient's Australian bank account in two AU$10,000 instalments after the census date of each semester of the first year of study. Up to two scholarships are available, offered across a December round and, if unawarded, a January round. Successful applicants must also participate in a Medibank industry-experience programme including an induction session, a guided tour of Medibank Head Office, Medibank workshops, Open Day event-coordination and a customer focus group.

award_types: Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship (AU$20,000, up to 2 awards)
Medibank Excellence Scholarship (AU$12,000, up to 5 awards)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: RMIT runs two Medibank-sponsored international scholarships for students completing Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia: the Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship (AU$20,000 in two AU$10,000 instalments, up to two awards) and the Medibank Excellence Scholarship (AU$12,000 in two AU$6,000 instalments, up to five awards). Both share identical eligibility criteria, open/close dates, terms and conditions and the same application form.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: No renewal. Payment is limited to the first year of the eligible program, in two instalments after each semester census date.
programme_structure.intake: Semester 1 2027 only. Two selection rounds: December round (closes Friday 18 December 2026) and January round (closes 10 January, printed as 2026 on the official page).
programme_structure.sourcing_note: Australia Awards Scholarships, Commonwealth scholarships and RMIT research scholarships are administered separately and are not covered by the International Scholarships Terms and Conditions.

status_note: Applications opened on 31 July 2026 for Semester 1 2027 commencement. The December round closes Friday 18 December 2026; scholarships not awarded in that round may be offered in a January round. The scholarship cannot be deferred and must be taken up in Semester 1 2027. Next expected cycle: Semester 1 2028, with applications expected to open around late July 2027.
verification_type: Official university scholarship page read and cross-checked against RMIT international admissions and English-requirement pages
verification_notes: All award value, number of awards, eligibility, selection criteria, deadlines, terms and application steps were taken verbatim from the official RMIT scholarship page and its linked application form. The general terms and conditions were read from the RMIT International Scholarships Terms and Conditions page. English-language figures were taken from the RMIT English language proficiency tests table, which publishes tiered requirements by course rather than a single bachelor's threshold, so the entry-level undergraduate tier is recorded and flagged as course-specific. No time of day or timezone is published for the scholarship closing dates. The January round closing date is printed as 2026 on the official page while the January round notification date is 12 January 2027; the discrepancy is reproduced as printed and flagged.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Applications open 31 July 2026. December round closes Friday 18 December 2026. January round (only for unawarded scholarships) closes 10 January, printed as 2026 on the official page.
application_deadline.application_period: 31 July 2026 to 18 December 2026 (December round); January round 19 December 2026 to 10 January.
application_deadline.official_rule: Applications open 31 July 2026. Applications close: December round Friday 18 December 2026; January round Sunday 10 January 2026 (year as printed on the official page). No closing time of day or timezone is published. 'If not awarded to eligible applicants in the December round, the scholarships may be offered in the January round.' 'The scholarships will be offered on a rolling basis and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until all available scholarships are exhausted.'
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The December round closes Friday 18 December 2026 and awards are made on a rolling first-come, first-served basis, so early submission materially improves the chance of an award. No closing time of day is published, so submit well before the end of the closing date. Any scholarships left unawarded after the December round may be released in a January round, so a missed December deadline does not necessarily remove all chance of an award, but the recipient pool is then much smaller.

programme_duration.official_range: First year of the eligible Associate degree or Bachelor degree program only (Semester 1 2027 and Semester 2 2027)
programme_duration.renewal_note: Not renewable. The total value is paid in two instalments after the census date of each semester of the first year. Under the general RMIT International Scholarships Terms and Conditions, scholarship duration is the standard full-time duration of the program or the minimum credit points required to graduate, whichever comes first; for this award the official page limits payment to the first year.

funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend is paid. The value is paid as two lump-sum instalments of AU$10,000 after the census date of each semester of the first year.
funding.living_allowance: AU$20,000 total cash stipend. The official page does not designate this as a living allowance; it is an unrestricted payment to the recipient's Australian bank account.
funding.fully_funded_note: This is not a fully funded award. It is a one-year AU$20,000 cash stipend and does not cover tuition fees, Overseas Student Health Cover, travel, accommodation or other costs. Recipients pay full international tuition fees.

tuition.note: Not a tuition fee waiver or fee offset. Recipients pay full international tuition fees; the award is a cash stipend paid to the recipient's Australian bank account.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. Payment is by lump-sum instalment, not monthly.

stipend_lump_sum.conditions: Paid in two AU$10,000 instalments after the census date of each semester of the first year. Recipients must provide bank details by the required date.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. Applicants must hold or intend to apply for a student visa, but no visa support is provided by the scholarship.

insurance.note: Not published in official source. Medibank is identified as the preferred Overseas Student Health Cover provider for RMIT international students, but the scholarship does not state that it covers OSHC.

research_allowance.note: Not applicable to a bachelor's stipend scholarship

bond.note: No service bond is stated. Recipients are instead required to participate in Medibank industry-experience activities: an induction session with a guided tour of Medibank Head Office, Medibank workshops, event-coordination for Medibank on Open Day, meeting recent Medibank graduates, and involvement in a customer focus group. RMIT or Medibank may profile scholarship recipients. These obligations are not a bond and do not create a repayment obligation.

total_estimated_value.note: Official published value of the scholarship. This is not an estimate of the total cost or total value of study; tuition, OSHC and living costs are additional and not covered.

coverage: Cash stipend of AU$20,000, paid in two AU$10,000 instalments after the census date of each semester of the first year of study

Medibank industry-experience opportunity: attendance at Medibank workshops, event-coordination for Medibank on Open Day, meeting recent graduates working at Medibank, and involvement in a customer focus group
Induction session including a guided tour of Medibank Head Office
Possible profiling of recipients by RMIT or Medibank
coverage_limitations: Covers the first year of study only. No renewal, second-year or subsequent-year funding is published.
Does not cover tuition fees. Recipients pay full international tuition fees, which are set per program and can be increased by RMIT by no more than 7.5% each calendar year.
Does not cover Overseas Student Health Cover, travel, accommodation, books, equipment or other living costs. No allowance for these is published.
The scholarship is not refundable and cannot be deferred to another year or intake.
Recipients must not be in receipt of any other RMIT scholarship, so the award cannot be stacked with other RMIT funding.
Payment is contingent on the recipient maintaining an active full-time enrolment; the scholarship is suspended during any leave of absence and is terminated if the student withdraws.
The exact benefit structure and terms may be changed by RMIT without notice, and unawarded scholarships in the December round may be released in a January round with the same terms.
eligible_applicants: Current Year 12 students in Australia graduating in 2026, or students completing the International Baccalaureate in Australia
International students holding a valid student visa or planning to apply for one before program commencement
Students who submit an application via VTAC and receive an offer from RMIT for an Associate degree or Undergraduate (Bachelor) degree
New students who are not existing RMIT students
final_year_condition: Eligibility is based on secondary completion, not a completed bachelor's degree. The applicant must be a current Year 12 student in Australia graduating in 2026, or completing the International Baccalaureate in Australia, and must receive an offer from RMIT for an Associate or Undergraduate degree for Semester 1 2027.
equivalent_degree_note: The official page names Australian Year 12 and the International Baccalaureate in Australia as the qualifying school-leaving qualifications. RMIT additionally recognises equivalent senior secondary qualifications for admission under its country and region equivalency rules, but the scholarship page does not publish a definitive list of equivalent school-leaving qualifications, so this is recorded as an assumption requiring confirmation with Study@RMIT.

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction. The scholarship is open to international students of any country. It is not restricted to nationals of any particular region.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must be applying from Australia and must be studying Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Current Year 12 student in Australia graduating in 2026, or completing the International Baccalaureate in Australia.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Applicants should achieve an ATAR higher than 90. The International Baccalaureate is an eligible qualification but no IB points threshold is published. Academic merit is a stated selection criterion.
eligibility.language_requirement: Applicants must meet the English language requirements of their chosen RMIT course. The entry-level undergraduate tier is IELTS (Academic) 6.5 with no band less than 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79, or PTE (Academic) 58, but requirements vary by course and may be higher. Australian Year 12 students can meet the requirement through English or EAL/ESL study scores.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required. No work experience criterion is published.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Applicants should show participation in extracurricular or leadership activities, or engagement in community or volunteer work. This is a selection criterion, not a strict eligibility condition.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Leadership participation is one of the stated selection criteria but is not framed as a mandatory eligibility condition.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Applicants must not be in receipt of any other RMIT scholarship. The scholarship is available only to non-existing RMIT students, so it cannot be transferred to a current student.
eligibility.previous_award_restriction: Applicants must not be in receipt of any other RMIT scholarship. The award also cannot be held by an existing RMIT student, and cannot be transferred to another university or person. No other limit on repeat application to the same award is published.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applicants must not be existing RMIT students. Recipients must maintain an active, full-time enrolment; continuing eligibility is assessed each semester.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Open to Associate degree and Undergraduate (Bachelor) degree programs at RMIT. Postgraduate, vocational and pathway programs are excluded. No discipline or field-of-study restriction is published for the degree itself.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No minimum percentage or GPA figure is published. The published academic threshold is an ATAR: applicants should achieve an ATAR higher than 90. This is a 'should' criterion rather than a stated hard cut-off, and no equivalent figure is published for International Baccalaureate applicants.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: RMIT publishes no scholarship-specific academic requirement per program. Course-level academic entry requirements apply separately and are stated on each program page.
selection_factors_may_include: Academic merit (ATAR above 90, or strong Year 12 / International Baccalaureate results for the Excellence tier)
Participation in extracurricular or leadership activities
Engagement in community or volunteer work
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is holistic and not based on marks alone: the official page states that 'Scholarship selection is based on academic merit, demonstrated involvement in extracurricular or community activities and personal qualities'. Applicants must submit a 200-word personal statement addressing these criteria.

english_requirement.moi_rule: RMIT may grant an exemption where the applicant's previous studies were taught and assessed entirely in English. For study completed outside a recognised English-speaking country, the applicant must have completed at least one year of a tertiary qualification equivalent to an Australian Diploma or higher within the past two years, one semester of full-time postgraduate study within the past two years, a recognised Bachelor degree or higher within the past five years, or a recognised senior secondary qualification within the past two years, and the course's IELTS requirement must be 6.5 or lower. Where a course requires IELTS 7.0 or above, a recognised English proficiency test must be provided even if previous study was in English. Australian Year 12 applicants can meet the undergraduate requirement with a VCE study score of at least 25 in English other than EAL, or at least 27 in ESL or EAL.
english_requirement.test_score_note: RMIT does not publish a single bachelor's English threshold. It publishes five IELTS-equivalent tiers (IELTS 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, and 8.0 with no band below 8.0) for 'Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Higher Degree by Research', and states that each course has specific minimum requirements which may differ even at the same study level, so applicants must check the individual course page. The entry-level undergraduate tier recorded above (IELTS 6.5 with no band less than 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79 with minimum 13 Reading, 12 Listening, 18 Speaking, 21 Writing, PTE (A) 58 with no communication band less than 50) is the most common requirement for undergraduate programs but is not universal.
accepted_tests: IELTS (Academic) and IELTS (Academic) One Skill Retake (IELTS General is not accepted)
TOEFL iBT (tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 must be the TOEFL iBT Australia test; 1-6 score-scale results are not accepted)
Occupational English Test (OET), accepted for selected health and medical science programs only
english_requirement.not_accepted: Duolingo English Test is not accepted by RMIT. Results from at-home or online tests are not accepted for international students.

language_of_instruction.language_note: RMIT teaches in English. The scholarship page does not state a language of instruction because it assumes English-language delivery; applicants must meet the English requirements of the specific RMIT course they are admitted to.

application_method.application_route: Two linked applications are required: (1) apply to RMIT for an Associate or Bachelor degree via VTAC and receive an offer; (2) submit a separate scholarship application form online.
application_steps: Step 1 - Choose your course: select an Associate or Undergraduate (Bachelor) degree at RMIT.
Step 2 - Apply via VTAC: submit your VTAC application to study at RMIT (https://vtac.edu.au/) and receive an offer.
Step 3 - Submit your scholarship application: complete the Medibank scholarship application form online.
Receive outcome: December round applicants are notified 23 December 2026; January round applicants are notified 12 January 2027. Unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
Accept the RMIT offer, including payment of applicable deposit fees, by Friday 8 January 2027 (December round) or Tuesday 26 January 2027 (January round).
application_method.application_fee: The official scholarship page states no scholarship application fee. RMIT states that applicants from select countries pay a non-refundable application fee, which is credited to the tuition fee deposit once the offer is accepted and the program commenced; the amount and country list are published separately. VTAC charges its own application fee, the amount of which is not stated on the RMIT scholarship page.

official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Not required at the scholarship application stage. Transcripts and graduation certificates are required by RMIT admissions as part of the course application.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Not stated on the scholarship application form. RMIT admissions requests academic transcripts and graduation certificates for the course application, with certified translations where the originals are not in English.

identity_documents.item: Passport details (implied by the student visa declaration and RMIT admissions process)
identity_documents.notes: The scholarship application form itself collects only name, email, VTAC ID, date of birth and a student visa declaration. It has no file-upload fields.
Form question: 'Are you holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement?' - yes/no dropdown.

The field is labelled 'ATAR score (if known)'. Applicants should aim for an ATAR higher than 90.

academic_documents.notes: Submitted to RMIT through the admissions/VTAC process, not uploaded to the scholarship form.

language_documents.notes: Required by RMIT admissions if the applicant does not meet the English requirement through an Australian Year 12 result or a recognised medium-of-instruction qualification. Test must have been completed within two years of the course start date.

recommendation_documents.notes: Not requested. The application form contains no recommendation fields or uploads.

financial_documents.notes: No financial documentation is requested. The scholarship is merit-based, not means-tested.

Required to receive the AU$10,000 instalments; under the general RMIT International Scholarships Terms and Conditions, failure to provide bank details by a required date may result in the scholarship being terminated or suspended for a semester.

RMIT offer letter for an Associate or Undergraduate degree for Semester 1 2027

selection_process.decision_maker: RMIT University Sponsorship Development Team, in conjunction with Medibank as sponsor
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive, holistic, and offered on a rolling first-come, first-served basis
possible_stages: Submission of the VTAC course application and receipt of an RMIT offer
Submission of the separate scholarship application form with personal statement
Assessment against academic merit, extracurricular or community involvement, and personal qualities
Rolling, first-come, first-served award until available scholarships are exhausted
Notification and acceptance of the RMIT offer with payment of applicable deposit fees
Induction session and Medibank industry-experience activities
selection_process.weighting_note: RMIT publishes no numerical weighting between academic merit, extracurricular or community involvement, and personal qualities. The official page lists these as the basis of selection without allocating percentages.
selection_process.results_timing: December round successful applicants are notified on 23 December 2026 and must accept their RMIT offer, including payment of applicable deposit fees, by Friday 8 January 2027. January round successful applicants are notified on 12 January 2027 and must accept by Tuesday 26 January 2027. Unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: No ranking list or score is published. Up to two scholarships are available, so the award pool is small; the official terms state awards are made on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis until all available scholarships are exhausted.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Personal qualities are a stated selection factor. Applicants must submit a 200-word personal statement addressing academic achievements, extracurricular activities, community involvement and personal qualities.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: RMIT Associate degree or Bachelor degree, as offered to the individual student
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship funds the first year of an RMIT Associate degree or Bachelor degree commencing in Semester 1 2027. The standard length of individual RMIT degrees is not stated on the scholarship page; applicants must check the specific program page. RMIT Higher Education Semester 1 2027 classes begin on 1 March 2027.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: RMIT offers credit for previous study, which applicants can request as part of the international application process. The scholarship page states no rule on whether credit affects the scholarship, and under the general International Scholarships Terms and Conditions the scholarship duration does not extend for credit.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients pay full international tuition fees. This scholarship is a cash stipend, not a fee waiver. RMIT may increase fees by no more than 7.5% each calendar year, subject to rounding. Tuition fees do not include the Student Services and Amenities Fee or material and other fees.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No scholarship-specific application fee is stated. Applicants from select countries pay a non-refundable RMIT application fee, which is credited to the tuition fee deposit once the offer is accepted and the program commenced.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Scholarship recipients are bound by the individual scholarship terms and conditions on the Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship page and by the RMIT International Scholarships Terms and Conditions, which apply to scholarships administered by the Sponsorship Development Team. RMIT may make changes to these terms and conditions without notice.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients receive an induction session including a guided tour of Medibank Head Office, and access to Medibank workshops, Open Day event-coordination, meetings with recent Medibank graduates, and a customer focus group. Standard RMIT international student services apply; Medibank is identified as the preferred Overseas Student Health Cover provider for RMIT international students.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond or service obligation is stated. Recipients are required to participate in Medibank industry-experience activities and may be profiled by RMIT or Medibank. These obligations do not create a repayment or service bond.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Under the general International Scholarships Terms and Conditions, a scholarship may be terminated if the student does not meet the eligibility criteria or terms and conditions, is suspended or excluded for misconduct, breaches RMIT policies or laws, provides false or misleading information, withdraws from the program, ceases to hold international status, or is overpaid. In most cases RMIT will request repayment if the scholarship has been overpaid. Where a scholarship is paid as a stipend and the student cancels after the semester has started and payment has been made, the student will be required to repay the Sponsorship Development Team. This particular scholarship is not refundable and cannot be deferred.

programme_comparison_fields: Award value: AU$20,000 (High Achiever) versus AU$12,000 (Excellence)
Number of awards: up to 2 (High Achiever) versus up to 5 (Excellence)
Academic threshold: ATAR above 90 recommended (High Achiever); no numeric threshold published (Excellence)
Payment structure: two instalments of AU$10,000 (High Achiever) versus two instalments of AU$6,000 (Excellence), both after each semester census date
Both awards: first year only, separate application required, same form, same eligibility, same deadlines, no stacking with other RMIT scholarships
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The personal statement is capped at 200 words and answers the form prompt 'What makes you an ideal candidate for this scholarship?'. The instruction is to highlight academic achievements, extracurricular activities, community involvement, and any personal qualities or experiences that set you apart. Because there is no interview, portfolio or document upload, this statement plus the ATAR is the entire discretionary case. Allocate roughly: one third to academic achievement, one third to extracurricular, leadership, community or volunteer commitment with concrete roles and duration, and one third to personal qualities and motivation aligned with Medibank's health-insurance focus. Because awards are made on a rolling first-come, first-served basis, submit as early as possible rather than polishing the statement for weeks.
profile_fit_labels: Strong academic performer targeting ATAR above 90
International student completing Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia
Student with extracurricular, leadership, community or volunteer track record
Student seeking a Medibank industry connection, networking and work-experience exposure
Student wanting a cash stipend rather than a tuition fee waiver, with family or sponsor funds available for tuition
common_mistakes: Assuming the scholarship is automatic on admission - a separate online application form is required
Applying directly to RMIT instead of through VTAC - the scholarship terms require a VTAC application and an RMIT offer
Using a different email address on the scholarship form than on the VTAC application
Applying as a student located outside Australia - applicants must be applying from Australia and studying Year 12 or the IB in Australia
Applying to a postgraduate, vocational or pathway program - only Associate and Bachelor degrees are eligible
Assuming the award can be deferred or renewed - it covers the first year only and cannot be deferred to another year or intake
Assuming the AU$20,000 covers tuition - it is a cash stipend and does not reduce tuition fees
Holding or applying for another RMIT scholarship - applicants must not be in receipt of any other RMIT scholarship
Waiting until the last day - awards are made on a rolling first-come, first-served basis until the pool is exhausted
Expecting a document upload to strengthen the application - the form has no upload fields, so the ATAR and personal statement carry the case

risk_flags.risk: Awards are made on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis until the pool of up to two scholarships is exhausted
risk_flags.impact: Late applicants may find no scholarships remain even though the published closing date has not passed, and the effective window may be much shorter than the published dates suggest
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit the scholarship application form as soon as it opens (31 July 2026) rather than waiting for the ATAR or the December round

risk_flags.risk: The AU$20,000 is a cash stipend, not a tuition fee waiver
risk_flags.impact: Applicants who assume tuition is covered may accept an RMIT place without funding for fees, which run to tens of thousands of Australian dollars per year
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget for full international tuition fees, the Student Services and Amenities Fee, Overseas Student Health Cover and living costs separately, and check the per-program fee on the RMIT program page

risk_flags.risk: Applicants must not be in receipt of any other RMIT scholarship
risk_flags.impact: Accepting this award disqualifies the applicant from other RMIT scholarships, including other Medibank tiers
risk_flags.mitigation: Compare the Medibank High Achiever (AU$20,000) and Medibank Excellence (AU$12,000) awards and RMIT's other international scholarships before applying, and confirm current rules with Study@RMIT

risk_flags.risk: Eligibility is limited to students completing Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia and applying from Australia
risk_flags.impact: Offshore international applicants are ineligible, which makes this an unusual fit for most international applicants using an overseas school-leaving qualification
risk_flags.mitigation: Offshore applicants should consider RMIT's other international scholarships such as the Future Leaders Scholarship (India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan), the Academic Merit Scholarship for South East Asia, or the Academic Merit Scholarship for Africa

risk_flags.risk: The ATAR threshold of 'higher than 90' is a 'should' criterion with no published minimum for International Baccalaureate applicants
risk_flags.impact: Applicants may invest effort in an application for which they are academically not competitive, or IB applicants may have no clear benchmark
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm competitiveness with Study@RMIT before applying and, for IB applicants, ask what equivalent result RMIT treats as meeting the threshold

risk_flags.risk: No closing time of day or timezone is published for the scholarship deadlines
risk_flags.impact: A submission made late on the closing date may miss the cut-off without the applicant knowing the official interpretation
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit at least several days before 18 December 2026 and retain the FormAssembly confirmation

risk_flags.risk: The January round closing date is printed as 10 January 2026 while the January round notification is 12 January 2027
risk_flags.impact: The printed date is inconsistent with the 2027 entry cycle and may cause applicants to mis-time a January round submission
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the January round as closing on or about 10 January 2027 and confirm the exact date with Study@RMIT before relying on it

risk_flags.risk: The award cannot be deferred, is not refundable, and is terminated if the student withdraws, takes a leave of absence, or loses international status
risk_flags.impact: A change of plan can leave the student with a terminated scholarship and a potential repayment obligation if instalments have already been paid
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the RMIT International Scholarships Terms and Conditions before accepting, and note that continuing eligibility is assessed each semester and full-time enrolment must be maintained

best_fit: An international student completing Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia, applying from Australia, with an ATAR above 90, a strong record of extracurricular, leadership, community or volunteer involvement, and a clear interest in working in health insurance or a comparable professional services field. Best suited to applicants who can fund tuition independently and want a substantial first-year cash stipend plus industry exposure at Medibank.
not_best_fit: Applicants applying from outside Australia or holding an overseas school-leaving qualification - eligibility requires Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate studied in Australia
Applicants who need tuition fees to be waived rather than receiving a cash payment
Applicants already studying at RMIT - existing students are not eligible

database_notes: Target selection: the brief asked for RMIT University international undergraduate scholarships and RMIT international fee-offset/scholarship schemes. RMIT's International Tuition Fee Scholarships (RIFOS and RRITFS) cover higher degree by research candidates only, so they are out of bachelor's scope. Among the coursework international scholarships, the Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship was chosen because it is open to international students of any nationality. The Future Leaders Scholarship, RMIT Academic Merit Scholarship for South East Asia and the Academic Merit Scholarship for Africa were excluded from consideration because they are locked to nationals of South Asia or Africa, which the research protocol treats as excluded regions; the Academic Excellence Scholarship for Central Asia and Mongolia is likewise nationality-locked.
No substitution was required. RMIT University was not on the do-not-duplicate list, and the assigned target was researched as briefed.

This record covers the Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship only. RMIT also runs a sibling award, the Medibank Excellence Scholarship (AU$12,000, up to five awards, no numeric ATAR threshold), which shares identical eligibility, deadlines, terms and application form but has lower priority because it offers less money.
short_title: RMIT publishes no acronym for this award. 'Medibank High Achiever' is a clear short form derived from the official name, used because no real acronym exists.
legacy_titles is empty. No former or alternative name for this award was found on official RMIT pages.

worldwide_eligibility is false: although there is no nationality restriction, applicants must be applying from Australia and must be studying Australian Year 12 or the International Baccalaureate in Australia. citizenship_restriction is false because no nationality is excluded.

bachelor_requirement is false in the Erasmus Mundus sense used by this schema: the award funds a bachelor's degree and does not require a completed bachelor's degree. Qualification at entry is secondary school completion.

degree_levels includes 'Associate degree' because the official eligibility wording admits both an Associate degree and an Undergraduate (Bachelor) degree. An RMIT Associate degree sits below ISCED Level 6; the Bachelor degree is ISCED Level 6.

The January round closing date is printed as 'Sunday 10 January 2026' on the official RMIT page, while the January round notification date is 12 January 2027. The year as printed is reproduced verbatim and flagged; the working assumption is that the intended year is 2027.
No closing time of day or timezone is published for either scholarship round. deadline_timezone is therefore null and no time is asserted.

The ATAR criterion is worded as 'Applicants should achieve an ATAR higher than 90' rather than a strict eligibility requirement. It is recorded as the published academic benchmark but is not presented as a guaranteed cut-off.

English-language scores were taken from RMIT's English language proficiency tests table for 'Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Higher Degree by Research'. RMIT publishes five tiers rather than a single bachelor's threshold and explicitly states that requirements may differ between courses at the same study level, so the entry-level tier (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 79 / PTE (A) 58) is recorded with the caveat that it is not scholarship-specific and not universal. RMIT does not accept the Duolingo English Test, and does not accept at-home or online test results for international students.

RMIT's general International Scholarships Terms and Conditions page does not state an appeal or review process for scholarship termination decisions, and does not state a prohibition on holding multiple scholarships. Only the individual Medibank scholarship terms bar the recipient from holding any other RMIT scholarship.
